subject: RetailCo vector migration & integration checklist — next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@retailco.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@retailco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: RetailCo vector migration & integration checklist — post-call recap

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — really helpful to see your current search+recommendation flow and the constraints around latency and accuracy. Per our discussion, I captured the integration items we agreed on and the immediate next steps so your engineering team can validate against the migration plan. Please see the short checklist and let me know if anything is off.

High-level recap:
- Current provider: Vectra (dense vectors, 512 dims)
- Goal: migrate embeddings to Redwood + run reranker integration for top-k re-ranking
- SLO: 100ms P95 end-to-end for embeddings->index->rerank path for single-query flows

Immediate technical checklist (action owners in parens):
1) Vector dimension & normalization: confirm if you want to keep 512 dims or reduce to 384 for cost/latency tradeoff (RetailCo infra)
2) Batching strategy: set client-side batching vs server-side batching thresholds and preferred batch window (RetailCo infra + Redwood)
3) Auth & routing: test API key flow and region routing we discussed (so us-east-1 by default) (Alex)
4) Structured output/tool calling: sample schema for reranker scoring payloads (output: score, explanation, token-span references) (Priya)
5) Migration plan: snapshot export format from Vectra (jsonl with base64 vectors ok) and roll-forward plan (see attached plan) (RetailCo)

Attachments:
- retailco_migration_plan.xlsx (migration milestones, data volumes, rollback criteria)
- retailco_current_vectors_sample.json (10k sample vectors, schema)

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: confirm vector dims preference and share export sample if you have any rows > 4096 tokens (by EOD Wed)
- Priya: share a representative query distribution + any banned tokens/normalization rules (by Thu)
- Marissa/Rishi: we'll stand up a short integration runbook and a test harness for auth/routing checks and a quick-lab to validate latency once we have sample vectors (we can do a 2-hour run the week of Dec 7)

If agreeable, I'll send a calendar invite for the integration run and loop in a Redwood infra engineer for the first 30 minutes to help with auth and routing smoke tests.

Thanks —
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retailco_migration_plan.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]
[Attachment: retailco_current_vectors_sample.json (json, 120KB)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@retailco.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@retailco.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RetailCo vector migration & integration checklist — post-call recap

Soojin,

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Dimension: we're leaning toward keeping 512 for parity with existing models, but we're open to a 384 A/B if Redwood's latency gains are material. Can your team produce a quick P95 comparison for 512 vs 384 with similar tokenization?
- Export: attached a small sample of our production export (jsonl with base64 vectors, 100 records). Note: a handful of vectors are sparse (lots of zeros) due to document trimming.
- Batching: our current client batches up to 32 vectors per upload; server-side batching would be fine if we can limit batch duration to 75ms for live inserts.
- Auth: we'll try the API key flow. For routing, prefer us-east-1 for initial proofing; we may add eu-west-1 later.

We'd like the integration run on Dec 8 (afternoon ET) if that works.

Alex
Head of ML Engineering, RetailCo
[Attachment: retailco_export_sample_100.jsonl (jsonl, 56KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@retailco.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@retailco.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:36:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RetailCo vector migration & integration checklist — scheduling integration run & auth tests

Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the sample export and the batching notes. Rishi and I reviewed the sample vectors and sketched a lightweight plan for the Dec 8 integration run. Summary and pre-checks below.

Pre-checks (please confirm completed before run):
- Confirmed sample received and validated (we saw sparse vectors as you noted) — ok.
- Confirm that export uses L2-normalized embeddings or state if you want Redwood to normalize on ingest (RetailCo)
- Provide a small query workload (top 100 queries) and a target P95 latency objective we should aim for in the run (RetailCo)

Dec 8 run plan (60–90 minutes):
1) Auth & routing smoke test (15 min) — validate API key auth, regional routing to us-east-1, and fallback to global cluster if regional saturated (Soojin/Marissa)
2) Ingest pilot (20 min) — small bulk ingest (10k vectors) with two modes: keep 512 dims vs downsize to 384 (server will return ingest time & tokenized size) (RetailCo + Redwood)
3) Embeddings query & rerank validation (25 min) — run 100 queries, compute baseline recall vs Vectra sample, collect P95 and throughput numbers. Reranker will return structured output: score, matched_span (start,end), and explanation token-ids (Rishi)
4) Post-run sync (10 min) — compare results, define next steps for full-scale migration

Notes on normalization and reranker inputs (technical):
- If you want deterministic cosine comparisons across providers, please send un-normalized vectors and let us normalize on ingest. That avoids accidental double-normalization.
- For batching: client-side windowing up to 32 is fine. On Redwood we'll enable dynamic batching with a max window of 50ms; this should keep latency in check while getting throughput wins for bulk writes.
- Reranker: we'll accept a structured JSON response per candidate containing {"score":"float","explanation":"string","token_span":"start-end"}. We'll share a small SDK helper that parses these fields into your ranking pipeline.

Action items and owners:
- Alex: confirm normalization preference (normalize on ingest vs pre-normalized) and share top-100 queries (by Mon Dec 6).
- Priya: confirm Dec 8 time slot (we have 15:00 - 17:00 ET available) and whether infra@retailco.com should be on the call.
- Rishi: I'll work with you to finalize the SDK helper and provide the sample call/response payloads before the run.

I'll send the Dec 8 invite once Alex/Priya confirm and include a short runbook and the SDK snippet.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
